cards.name: Average
cards.summary: Finds the mean colour of the layer (or of the active selection) and fills that whole area with it, so the image is replaced by one flat, featureless colour. On the test plate the whole frame becomes a single warm mid brown (about RGB 132/104/74).
use_for: sampling the overall colour of a photo to build a matching background panel, text box or brand swatch
averaging a selected patch of skin, wall or sky to pick a clean fill colour for retouching
spotting a colour cast: average a duplicate layer and see whether the grey turns warm, green or blue, then neutralise it
a flat colour tile that sits next to a photo in a collage and matches it
avoid: it wipes out every detail of the area it touches: run it on a duplicate layer or inside a selection, never on the only copy
a palette of several colours: Average gives just one; use Mosaic, Pixelate or the Color Theme / swatch tools for a palette
averaging a selection that crosses very different areas gives a muddy compromise colour: select one area at a time
pairs_with: a selection (averages only that area)
Blend mode Color or Overlay (tints a layer with the averaged colour)
Eyedropper Tool (to read the averaged value)
cards.scripting: executeAction(charIDToTypeID('Avrg'), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO);  // no params; the harvest found no stringID for this event, so use the charID
cards.non_destructive: yes: smart-filter capable (harvest applied it to a Smart Object and read the filterFX entry back); on a plain pixel layer it is destructive
cards.cost: light: one pass to compute the mean and one fill (279 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer)

verified.note: Frame and crop are one flat warm mid brown (132 / 104 / 74), exactly the value the card names.

cards.name: Blur
cards.summary: Applies a fixed, very light blur that smooths pixels next to hard edges and sharp colour transitions; there is no setting. On a large or already soft photo (like the test plate) the change is barely visible: only the crisp strip at the bottom, its hairlines and the white type lose a little edge.
use_for: taking the harsh edge off pixelated or stair-stepped lines, small type or a hard mask edge
slightly softening noise or JPEG artefacts on a small web graphic
repeated a few times as a quick, setting-free soften in an action
avoid: any blur that should be clearly seen: use Gaussian Blur or Box Blur, which have a Radius
large, high-resolution images: the fixed amount is tiny relative to the frame and looks like nothing happened
noise reduction on a photo: Reduce Noise or Surface Blur keep detail better
pairs_with: Blur More (the same idea, stronger)
Gaussian Blur (when a controllable amount is needed)
Sharpen (the opposite direction)
cards.non_destructive: yes: smart-filter capable (harvest applied it to a Smart Object and read the filterFX entry back); on a plain pixel layer it is destructive
cards.cost: light: a single small-kernel pass (123 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer)

verified.note: 960 frame unchanged by eye; on the 1:1 crop the hairlines, bar edges and type lose a little edge (detail 9.9 vs 13.6) while the soft photo barely moves, the faint fixed blur described.

cards.name: Blur More
cards.summary: The same fixed, setting-free light blur as Blur, only stronger. On the 1920 px test plate it is still faint: the photo barely changes and only up close do the hairlines, colour-block edges and white type look softer; it never reads as out of focus.
use_for: a quick soften of a small graphic, icon or thumbnail without opening a dialog
smoothing jagged edges or speckle on a low-resolution screenshot or scan
a setting-free soften step inside a recorded action
avoid: a strong or exactly repeatable blur: use Gaussian Blur with a Radius
large photos: on high-resolution images the fixed amount is small and easy to miss
depth-of-field or background blur: use Lens Blur or the Blur Gallery's Field / Iris Blur
pairs_with: Blur (weaker)
Gaussian Blur (controllable)
Unsharp Mask (to restore edge contrast afterwards)
cards.scripting: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("blurMethod"), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO);  // no params; the harvested event stringID is "blurMethod" (the stringID Photoshop reports for this command's code); it ran on the harvest's test layer with an empty descriptor
cards.non_destructive: yes: smart-filter capable (harvest applied it to a Smart Object and read the filterFX entry back); on a plain pixel layer it is destructive
cards.cost: light: a single small-kernel pass (106 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer)

review.changes: summary: removed the un-harvested 'three to four times' figure and the 'noticeably softer' overclaim (faint on the 1920 plate); scripting comment no longer claims more than the harvest showed

verified.note: Faint as described: the 1:1 crop's hairlines and block edges are visibly softer than with Blur (detail 5.8 vs 9.9) while the photo looks unchanged in the 960 frame.

cards.name: Box Blur
cards.summary: Blurs each pixel to the plain average of a square of neighbours Radius pixels around it, so detail melts evenly; compared with Gaussian Blur the falloff is flatter and harder, and at large radii bright spots and edges spread into soft square-ish smears. With a big Radius the test plate turns into a heavy, slightly blocky colour haze.
use_for: a strong, even background blur behind a headline or panel when a slightly flatter look than Gaussian is fine
a stylised, boxy soft-focus or frosted look for a poster background
smoothing a mask or displacement map evenly before using it
a fast heavy blur on large images (very large radii are allowed)
avoid: a natural, round falloff (glows, soft shadows, photo backgrounds): Gaussian Blur or Lens Blur look smoother
small radii on an already soft photo look like nothing happened: go clearly bigger, or use it on sharp art
the edges of a layer with transparency fade and bleed: lock transparency or fill the layer first

params.name: Radius
params.does: half-width of the square that is averaged, in pixels (harvest range 1-2000); bigger = stronger, flatter blur
params.typical: 3-10 for a soft background, 20-60 for a heavy wash

pairs_with: Gaussian Blur (smoother alternative)
a layer mask (keeps the subject sharp)
Add Noise (puts grain back on a smooth blurred area)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("radius"), stringIDToTypeID("pixelsUnit"), 25); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("boxblur"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // radius is clamped by Photoshop to 1..2000; the harvest recorded no unit for this radius, pixelsUnit is assumed (Gaussian and Shape Blur radius read back in pixels)
cards.non_destructive: yes: smart-filter capable (harvest applied it to a Smart Object and read the filterFX entry back); on a plain pixel layer it is destructive (radius is stored with it)
cards.cost: light: fast even at large radii (136 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer)

review.changes: scripting comment: dropped the un-harvested 'Photoshop's own recording uses pixelsUnit' claim, now says pixelsUnit is an assumption

verified.note: Heavy even blur, the hairlines melt into a grey band and bright spots spread into square-ish smears on the 1:1 crop.

cards.name: Gaussian Blur
cards.summary: The standard adjustable blur: each pixel is averaged with its neighbours using a bell-shaped weighting, so detail, type and hairlines melt into a smooth haze with no hard artefacts; Radius sets how far it spreads. On the already soft test plate a radius of a dozen pixels or more is needed before mid-tone detail and type clearly dissolve.
use_for: blurring a photo background behind a headline, card or lower-third so the text reads
a frosted-glass panel: blur a copy of the image inside the panel shape
soft drop shadows and glows: blur a filled copy of the shape or type
softening a mask edge or a displacement map
abstract colour-wash backgrounds made from a photo at a very large radius
avoid: a realistic out-of-focus camera look with bokeh: use Lens Blur or the Blur Gallery's Field / Iris Blur
blurring the whole frame of a news photo: it reads as a mistake; mask it to the background
noise reduction or skin smoothing: Surface Blur, Smart Blur or Reduce Noise keep edges
the edges of a layer with transparency fade into a soft halo: lock transparency or blur a merged copy

params.name: Radius
params.does: how far the blur spreads, in pixels (harvest range 0.1-1000)
params.typical: 0.5-2 px subtle soften, 5-20 px background blur, 40-200 px colour wash

pairs_with: a layer mask (keeps the subject sharp)
Screen or Soft Light blend mode on a blurred copy (glow / Orton look)
Add Noise (matches grain over the blurred area)
High Pass (the inverse: keeps what Gaussian removes)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("radius"), stringIDToTypeID("pixelsUnit"), 18); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("gaussianBlur"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // radius is clamped by Photoshop to 0.1..1000 px
cards.non_destructive: yes: smart-filter capable (harvest applied it to a Smart Object and read the filterFX entry back); on a plain pixel layer it is destructive (radius is stored with it)
cards.cost: light to medium: fast at small radii, slower at very large radii on big images (139 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer)

verified.note: Smooth bell-shaped haze over the whole frame with no hard artefacts; the hairlines melt into flat grey on the 1:1 crop and the type dissolves.

cards.name: Lens Blur
cards.summary: Imitates a real camera's shallow depth of field: the image is blurred with an iris-shaped kernel so bright highlights bloom into shaped bokeh discs, and an optional depth map (Depth Image Target Layer or Alpha Channel) decides what stays sharp at the Focal Distance. With Depth Image None the whole frame goes evenly out of focus; on the test plate the Specular settings make the white type, hairlines and small bright highlights bloom, and Noise puts grain back.
use_for: a realistic out-of-focus background behind a cut-out person, product or headline
faking shallow depth of field on a flat photo with a gradient or painted alpha channel as depth map
bokeh-style highlights from lights, candles or city lights for a festive or night poster
a blurred background plate that keeps film grain (Noise Amount) so it matches the sharp subject
avoid: it cannot be applied as a Smart Filter (harvest: the command is not available on a Smart Object): work on a duplicate layer
it is slow on large images, and extreme values kept Photoshop busy for over 9 minutes in the harvest probe: stay inside the dialog ranges
a quick even blur: Gaussian Blur is much faster
a depth-of-field look without a depth map blurs everything evenly: paint an alpha channel or use the Blur Gallery's Tilt-Shift / Field Blur instead
the harvest could not read min/max for any setting: keep values inside the dialog's ranges

params.name: Depth Image
params.does: source of the depth map: None (uniform blur), Target Layer or Alpha Channel (the dialog's Source menu; which mask or channel is used is not recorded by the harvest)
params.typical: None for an even background blur; an alpha channel gradient for a depth-of-field fake

params.name: Focal Distance
params.does: the depth-map grey level that stays sharp (an integer; no range was probed)
params.typical: 0 or the grey of the subject area; only matters with a depth map

params.name: Inverted Map
params.does: flips the depth map so near and far swap
params.typical: false

params.name: Iris Shape
params.does: number of aperture blades, which sets the outline of the bokeh highlights
params.typical: Hexagon (default) or Octagon for rounder discs

params.name: Iris Radius
params.does: amount of blur (size of the aperture)
params.typical: 15-40 for a background, 50-80 for a heavy defocus

params.name: Blade Curvature
params.does: rounds the iris blades so the bokeh discs become circular

params.name: Iris Rotation
params.does: rotates the iris shape, so the bokeh polygon tilts

params.name: Specular Brightness
params.does: how much the brightest areas are boosted into glowing bokeh

params.name: Specular Threshold
params.does: brightness level above which pixels are treated as specular highlights (lower = more of the image blooms)

params.name: Noise Amount
params.does: grain added back over the blur so it matches the unblurred parts

params.name: Noise Distribution
params.does: Uniform or Gaussian grain
params.typical: Gaussian

params.name: Monochromatic Noise
params.does: grain without colour speckles
params.typical: true for a natural film grain

pairs_with: an alpha channel or layer mask gradient (the depth map)
Select Subject + layer mask (keeps the person sharp on top)
Add Noise (if Noise Amount is not used)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putEnumerated(charIDToTypeID('BkDi'), charIDToTypeID('BtDi'), charIDToTypeID('BeIn')); d.putInteger(charIDToTypeID('BkDp'), 0); d.putBoolean(charIDToTypeID('BkDs'), false); d.putEnumerated(charIDToTypeID('BkIs'), charIDToTypeID('BtIs'), charIDToTypeID('BeS6')); d.putDouble(charIDToTypeID('BkIb'), 50); d.putInteger(charIDToTypeID('BkIc'), 0); d.putInteger(charIDToTypeID('BkIr'), 0); d.putDouble(charIDToTypeID('BkSb'), 40); d.putInteger(charIDToTypeID('BkSt'), 200); d.putInteger(charIDToTypeID('BkNa'), 0); d.putEnumerated(charIDToTypeID('BkNt'), charIDToTypeID('BtNt'), charIDToTypeID('BeNu')); d.putBoolean(charIDToTypeID('BkNm'), false); executeAction(charIDToTypeID('Bokh'), d, DialogModes.NO);  // no stringIDs are registered for this plug-in: every key, enum type and value is a charID (from the harvest); no ranges were probed
cards.non_destructive: no: not smart-filter capable (harvest: applying it to a Smart Object failed with 'The command "Lens Blur" is not currently available'); it rewrites the pixel layer
cards.cost: heavy: 1153 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer (8x Gaussian Blur), much longer on full-size images and with large Iris Radius

review.changes: summary no longer claims Target Layer reads 'a layer's mask or transparency' (not in the harvest); removed the un-harvested 0-255 Focal Distance range and the 'up to about 100' Iris Radius ceiling

verified.note: Even defocus over the whole frame with the white type, hairlines and small bright highlights blooming into bright soft shapes; with Noise 0 no grain comes back.

cards.name: Motion Blur
cards.summary: Smears every pixel along one straight line, like a subject or camera moving during the exposure: Angle sets the direction and Distance the length of the streaks. Edges perpendicular to the angle streak most: with Angle 0 the large shapes, thin diagonal lines, the stripes and the colour-block borders smear sideways, while the horizontal hairlines and the grey ramp barely change.
use_for: speed and movement behind a sports, car or action cut-out
a dynamic streaked background for a sale or launch poster
speed lines on type or a logo copy placed under the sharp original
faking camera shake or panning on a still frame
avoid: both keys are required: Photoshop refused an empty descriptor in the harvest, so always send Angle and Distance

the harvest could not read a range for either key: every probe read back Angle 0 / Distance 10 because the result descriptor executeAction returns is not a read-back for this filter: it reports the dialog's last-used values (proven in the PS effect gallery: re-applying the reported values gives different pixels, the values sent reproduce the frame exactly), so judge a scripted run by its pixels: keep both to values the Motion Blur dialog accepts and check the result
pixels near the canvas edge streak in from beyond the border and look smeared: work on a larger canvas or crop afterwards
a zoom or spin movement: use Radial Blur, or the Blur Gallery's Path / Spin Blur for curved motion

params.name: Angle
params.does: direction of the streaks in degrees (0 = horizontal)
params.typical: 0 for horizontal speed, 90 for vertical fall, about 15-30 for a diagonal dash

params.name: Distance
params.does: length of the streaks in pixels
params.typical: 10-30 for a hint of motion, 50-150 for strong speed

pairs_with: a layer mask (keeps the front of the subject sharp)
Lighten or Screen blend mode on a blurred copy (speed trails behind the sharp subject)
Radial Blur (zoom variant)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("angle"), 0); d.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("distance"), stringIDToTypeID("pixelsUnit"), 60); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("motionBlur"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // send both keys: an empty descriptor fails
cards.non_destructive: not probed by the harvest (no smart-filter result recorded); Photoshop normally allows it as a Smart Filter on a Smart Object, but that is unconfirmed here; on a plain pixel layer it is destructive
cards.cost: medium: longer distances take longer (844 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer)

review.changes: summary: replaced 'vertical flagpoles' (none on the plate) with what is there; avoid: dropped the invented 'within one turn' range and noted the probe read-backs; non_destructive: smart-filter support marked unconfirmed; confidence high -> medium (no defaults or ranges, and the harvest's Angle 1 read back as 0)

verified.note: Horizontal streaks: vertical edges (stripes, block borders, the type) smear sideways while the horizontal hairlines stay crisp except at their ends; the stale read-back (distance 10) is not what was applied.

cards.name: Radial Blur
cards.summary: Blurs around a centre point in one of two ways: Spin smears pixels along circles as if the frame rotated (centre sharp, edges swirl), Zoom streaks them outward from the centre like a lens zooming during the exposure (a speed-burst tunnel). Amount sets the strength and Quality trades speed for smoothness.
use_for: a zoom-burst background that pulls the eye to the centre of a poster or thumbnail
spinning wheels, fans or rotating objects (Spin on a selection)
an energetic, explosive look behind a headline or a sports cut-out
avoid: Draft quality looks grainy and dotted: use Good or Best for final output

the centre is set in a dialog preview box, not on the image; a script that leaves center out reuses the last-used centre, so send it as the harvest read it back (a paint object with horizontal / vertical plain doubles, 0.5 / 0.5)
Best quality on large images is slow
straight-line movement: use Motion Blur; CorelDRAW splits this filter into Radial Blur (spin) and Zoom

params.name: Amount
params.does: strength of the spin or zoom (harvest range 1-100)
params.typical: Spin 5-20, Zoom 20-60

params.name: Method
params.does: spin (circular smear) or zoom (outward streaks)
params.typical: zoom for a speed burst, spin for rotation

params.name: Quality
params.does: draft (fast, grainy), good or best (smoothest, slowest)
params.typical: good; best for final print

params.name: Center
params.does: point the blur rotates or zooms around: a paint-class object with horizontal / vertical plain doubles (the harvest read back 0.5 / 0.5, the last-used value)
params.typical: horizontal 0.5, vertical 0.5 (the value the harvest read back)

pairs_with: a layer mask (keeps the subject sharp in the middle)
Lighten blend mode on a blurred copy (light rays)
Motion Blur (straight-line variant)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("amount"), 35); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("blurMethod"), stringIDToTypeID("blurMethod"), stringIDToTypeID("zoom")); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("blurQuality"), stringIDToTypeID("blurQuality"), stringIDToTypeID("good")); var c = new ActionDescriptor(); c.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("horizontal"), 0.5); c.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("vertical"), 0.5); d.putObject(stringIDToTypeID("center"), stringIDToTypeID("paint"), c); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("radialBlur"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // amount clamped to 1..100; center sent in the read-back format (paint object, plain doubles) so the last-used centre is not reused
cards.non_destructive: yes: smart-filter capable (harvest applied it to a Smart Object and read the filterFX entry back); on a plain pixel layer it is destructive
cards.cost: medium: Best quality and large Amount are slow on big images (315 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer)

review.changes: center: the harvest did record its format (paint object, plain doubles 0.5/0.5); omitting it reuses the LAST-USED centre, not the image centre, so avoid/params/scripting now send it

verified.note: Zoom streaks radiate outward from the frame centre, strongest at the edges, with the faint grain of Good quality on the 1:1 crop.

cards.name: Shape Blur
cards.summary: Blurs using a custom shape (chosen from the Custom Shape list in the dialog) as the blur kernel instead of a circle, so the blur gets the shape's character: bright spots and edges spread into the outline of the shape (heart, star, leaf ...). Radius sets the size of the kernel. Photoshop declares kernelType, customShape, pattern and brush keys too, but the harvest read back only Radius, so their value format is unknown and a script gets whatever shape the dialog last used.
use_for: decorative shaped bokeh (hearts, stars) on lights for a wedding, festive or greeting design
an unusual, graphic blur texture for a poster background
a stylised alternative to Gaussian Blur when a hint of pattern is wanted
avoid: precise control of the shape from a script: only Radius was harvested, so set the shape once in the dialog or record an action
the harvest could not read a range for Radius: stay inside the dialog's range
a plain, natural blur: Gaussian Blur or Lens Blur

expecting the shape on a soft photo: it prints only where small bright points sit on a dark ground (lights, sparkles); on the gallery plate neither Radius 30 nor 80 printed a visible outline, though the kernel recovered from the Radius 80 frame was the dialog's last-used custom shape (an animal silhouette), not a circle

params.name: Radius
params.does: size of the shape kernel in pixels; bigger = stronger blur and a more visible shape in highlights
params.typical: 10-30 for a soft blur, 40-100 for a heavy one; the outline shows only on small highlights

pairs_with: Custom Shape presets (choose the kernel shape in the dialog)
Lens Blur (round or polygon bokeh instead)
a layer mask (keeps the subject sharp)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("radius"), stringIDToTypeID("pixelsUnit"), 80); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("shapeBlur"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // only radius has a harvested format; the kernel shape stays at the dialog's last-used shape; the result descriptor executeAction returns is not a read-back for this filter: it reports the dialog's last-used values (proven in the PS effect gallery: re-applying the reported values gives different pixels, the values sent reproduce the frame exactly), so judge a scripted run by its pixels (the harvest's range probes read that descriptor, hence their constant 10)
cards.non_destructive: yes: smart-filter capable (harvest applied it to a Smart Object and read the filterFX entry back); on a plain pixel layer it is destructive (radius is stored with it)
cards.cost: light at small radii (107 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer), slower at large radii

review.changes: summary: no longer says the shape 'is not a settable key' (the batch declares kernelType / customShape / pattern / brush; only their format is unharvested); scripting warns the radius probes all read back 10

verified.note: Radius 80 gives a heavy blur with faint ghosted copies of the type, no visible shaped highlight; pixel fits rule out a box or disc kernel (best fits 8 levels off) and deconvolving the frame against the plate recovers an animal-silhouette custom shape (the dialog's last-used one) about 160 px across, so the shaped kernel is real, but this soft plate has no small point lights to print it visibly.

previous.note: A heavy even blur close to Box Blur (1:1 crop mean difference 8 levels from Box Blur, linear edge ramps) with no shaped bokeh anywhere: the soft plate has no isolated bright points for a shaped kernel to print, and the shape is the dialog's last-used one, so the shape character the card leads with cannot be judged here; demo Radius raised 30 -> 80 (the card's own 40-100 "to see the shape" range) for a rerender.

second_opinion.note: Re-opened frame + crop and zoomed the type and small bright highlights against Box Blur: near-identical soft smears, no shaped highlight. Plate check: the plate does have small bright highlights, white type and hairlines for a larger kernel to print its outline on, so this is a demo-strength limit, not a plate one. Harness check: the kernel is the dialog's last-used shape (no harvested value format for customShape), so the rerender tests whether a shape reads at all, not a chosen shape. Radius 80 has no harvested range against it (the range probe read the stale descriptor).

verified.second_opinion: plate limit, not demo strength: a bigger radius will not show the shape; it needs a plate with small bright points (or a settable customShape, whose value format is unharvested)

cards.name: Smart Blur
cards.summary: An edge-preserving blur: areas whose contrast is below Threshold are smoothed within Radius, while edges with more contrast stay crisp, so skin, walls and noise flatten into smooth, slightly posterised, painted-looking patches. Mode Edge Only replaces the image with white edge lines on black, Overlay Edge draws those white lines over the image.
use_for: reducing noise and blotchiness in a soft video frame while keeping outlines
a smooth, painted or cartoon-flat look on a photo for a poster or illustration base
quick skin smoothing (lower Radius and Threshold) on a small portrait
an outline drawing from a photo with Edge Only mode
avoid: high Threshold with a large Radius gives a plastic, posterised look and loses texture: lower them for natural results
a true out-of-focus blur: Gaussian Blur or Lens Blur
professional skin retouching: frequency separation or Surface Blur on a masked layer gives more control

params.name: Radius
params.does: how far the blur searches for similar pixels (harvest range 0.1-100)
params.typical: 3-10 for clean-up, 15-30 for a painted look

params.name: Threshold
params.does: how different neighbouring pixels may be and still be blurred together (harvest range 0.1-100); higher blurs across more edges
params.typical: 15-30 for clean-up, 40-60 for a flat painted look

params.name: Quality
params.does: Low, Medium or High: higher is smoother and slower
params.typical: High for final output

params.name: Mode
params.does: Normal (the blur), Edge Only (white edges on black) or Overlay Edge (white edges over the image)
params.typical: Normal

pairs_with: Add Noise (puts back texture after smoothing)
Unsharp Mask (re-crisps outlines)
Posterize or Cutout (stronger illustration look)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("radius"), 25); d.putDouble(stringIDToTypeID("threshold"), 50); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("smartBlurQuality"), stringIDToTypeID("smartBlurQuality"), stringIDToTypeID("smartBlurQualityHigh")); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("smartBlurMode"), stringIDToTypeID("smartBlurMode"), stringIDToTypeID("smartBlurModeNormal")); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("smartBlur"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // radius and threshold clamped by Photoshop to 0.1..100
cards.non_destructive: not probed by the harvest (no smart-filter result recorded); expected to work as a Smart Filter on a Smart Object like the other parameterised Blur filters, but unconfirmed here; on a pixel layer it is destructive
cards.cost: medium: High quality with a large radius is slow on big images (391 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer)

verified.note: Low-contrast areas flatten into smooth, slightly posterised painted patches while edges (panel rims, stripes, type, hairlines) stay crisp, clear on the 1:1 crop.
